target.title: fix(telegram): keep DM topic auto-rename user message UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who send long Telegram messages containing emoji as their first turn in a DM topic session would get a garbled or empty auto-renamed topic title.

OpenClaw can automatically rename Telegram forum topics on the first turn of a session. To do this it truncates the user's message to 500 characters and passes it to an LLM for label generation. The truncation uses `.slice(0, 500)`, which counts UTF-16 code units. Emoji and other characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane are represented as surrogate pairs (two UTF-16 code units). If such a character straddles the 500-unit boundary, the slice discards the second half of the pair, producing an isolated high surrogate — invalid Unicode.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace `.slice(0, 500)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(..., 500)`, which backs up one code unit when the cut point falls inside a surrogate pair. This helper is the established pattern for all user-text truncation in the codebase (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`).

## User Impact

Users sending emoji-heavy first messages in Telegram DM topic sessions (e.g. `"Hi 👋 tell me about 🦞🦞🦞 …"` long enough to reach 500 chars) would receive a malformed auto-topic label — either a replacement character, garbled output, or a rejected model call. After this fix the topic label is always derived from a valid Unicode string.

## Evidence

- **Affected path:** `extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.ts:3078` — `userMessage` is built with `truncateUtf16Safe(ctxPayload.RawBody ?? ctxPayload.Body ?? "", 500)` then passed to `generateTopicLabel({ userMessage, … })`.
- **Fix:** `truncateUtf16Safe(..., 500)` — same semantics, surrogate-safe boundary.
- **Pattern match:** `truncateUtf16Safe` is used in the same way throughout the Telegram plugin for other string limits (e.g. `raw-update-log.ts`) and was added for exactly this class of bug.
- **Diff:** one new import, one call-site replacement in `bot-message-dispatch.ts`; surrogate-boundary regression in `bot-message-dispatch.test.ts`.

### Behavior proof

#### 1) Node runtime boundary reproduction (exact `bot-message-dispatch.ts` expression, no mocks)

Uses the same input shape as the regression test (`499 × 'a' + 😀tail`) and the production truncation expression:

```text
=== Telegram DM topic auto-rename UTF-16 reproduction (Node runtime, bot-message-dispatch.ts logic, no mocks) ===
Node: v22.22.0
rawBody code units: 505
old .slice(0, 500) code units: 500
old userMessage has unpaired surrogate: true
old userMessage last char: U+D83D
truncateUtf16Safe(rawBody, 500) code units: 499
fixed userMessage has unpaired surrogate: false
fixed userMessage equals 499 ASCII a's: true
fixed userMessage would reach generateTopicLabel cleanly: true
```

This shows the before/after contract on the auto-topic label input path: emoji straddling the 500 cap is dropped whole instead of leaving `U+D83D` in `userMessage`.

#### 2) Call-site regression through production `dispatchTelegramMessage`

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/bot-message-dispatch.test.ts -t "truncates DM topic auto-rename" --reporter=verbose

 ✓ dispatchTelegramMessage draft streaming > truncates DM topic auto-rename input on UTF-16 boundaries

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  1 passed | 171 skipped (172)
```

Regression drives the real DM-topic auto-rename branch and asserts `generateTopicLabel` receives `userMessage` with length ≤ 500, no unpaired surrogate, and value exactly `499 × 'a'` for boundary input `499 × 'a' + 😀tail`.

**Proof gap:** No redacted live Telegram Desktop / Bot API transcript in this validation environment. Node reproduction plus the `dispatchTelegramMessage` regression cover the production truncation before `generateTopicLabel`; optional supplemental proof is a redacted first-turn DM topic rename showing a long emoji-near-boundary message produces a well-formed topic title.
